name: Save the Cat
description: Fifteen beats across three acts, popular for commercial fiction and screenplays.

acts.title: Act One
acts.description: The protagonist's world before the change, and the choice to leave it.

beats.name: Opening Image
beats.hint: A snapshot of the protagonist and their world before anything changes.

beats.name: Theme Stated
beats.hint: Someone hints at what the protagonist needs to learn, usually without them noticing.

beats.name: Set-Up
beats.hint: The protagonist's life, flaws and what is missing from it.

beats.name: Catalyst
beats.hint: The life-changing event that knocks the protagonist off course.

beats.name: Debate
beats.hint: The protagonist hesitates: should they go, and what will it cost?

acts.title: Act Two
acts.description: The new world: promise, trouble and the fall.

beats.name: Break into Two
beats.hint: The protagonist chooses to act and enters a new world or situation.

beats.name: B Story
beats.hint: A new relationship that will carry the theme.

beats.name: Fun and Games
beats.hint: The promise of the premise: the scenes the reader came for.

beats.name: Midpoint
beats.hint: A false victory or false defeat that raises the stakes.

beats.name: Bad Guys Close In
beats.hint: Pressure mounts from outside and doubts grow inside.

beats.name: All Is Lost
beats.hint: The worst moment: something or someone is lost.

beats.name: Dark Night of the Soul
beats.hint: The protagonist hits bottom and faces what they have been avoiding.

acts.title: Act Three
acts.description: The protagonist applies what they learned.

beats.name: Break into Three
beats.hint: A new idea, often from the B Story, shows the way forward.

beats.name: Finale
beats.hint: The protagonist puts the lesson into action and confronts the problem.

beats.name: Final Image
beats.hint: A mirror of the Opening Image that shows how much has changed.
